messages:
taylor_arch: quick idea — propose `pin_matrix` as a compact tenant->variant affinity table to replace sprawling per-tenant pins. trying to balance expressivity and storage/lookup cost.

alex_k: sketch it out pls, curious how it impacts resolver perf.

maria_dev: high-level concern: more compact is great, but we need to keep rollback semantics obvious for ops. if a matrix entry overrides a previous pin, how do we surface that?

pranav_s: also watch telemetry: we must still be able to attribute misses/evictions back to a concrete pin operation for postmortems. compact encodings can obfuscate provenance.

(taylor_arch uploads a snippet)

`taylor_arch: proto example:`
```json
{
  "pin_matrix_v1": {
    "columns": ["tenant", "env", "variant"],
    "rows": [
      ["acme", "prod", "v2-weight:0.8;v2-canary:0.2"],
      ["acme", "staging", "v1"],
      ["globex", "prod", "v3"]
    ],
    "meta": { "created_by": "release-bot", "epoch": 1736501000 }
  }
}
```

alex_k: I like the compactness. How would runtime lookups work? naive approach scans rows — O(n). we need an index map for (tenant,env) -> row pointer.

maria_dev: index map is fine, but then we reintroduce per-tenant state. maybe keep a bloom-ish prefix cache for hot tenants?

pranav_s: edge-case: tenant-level overrides. example: acme pinned v2, but for campaign acme/marketing we need an explicit hard pin. matrix should support scoped exceptions. maybe a small exception list keyed by (tenant, route).

alex_k: agree. also must ensure fallback ordering is deterministic: matrix entry, tenant-exception, global-default. document that in the resolver contract.

maria_dev: rollout plan question — how do we migrate existing pins? options: 1) one-time migration job to materialize into pin_matrix rows; 2) lazy co-existence where resolver reads both and prefers newest; 3) leave existing pins and translate only on write.

pranav_s: I vote lazy co-existence for safety. Resolver checks explicit pins first, then matrix. add a small compatibility TTL so old pins retire after X days.

(taylor_arch): okay, lazy co-existence seems lowest-risk. migration job optional for cleanup. will add `compat_ttl` field to metadata.

maria_dev: observability: telemetry keys we need: resolved_source (explicit_pin|matrix|default), matched_row_id, matrix_epoch, override_reason. also include referential pin_id if translated.

alex_k: perf bench notes: if index map + LRU cache used, lookups are ~1-2ms median. scanning cold matrix for rare tenants is acceptable if we keep rows compact. ensure we compress string blobs and prefer numeric IDs in storage.

pranav_s: security/ACLs: matrix edits should require stricter RBAC because they change many tenants at once. UI should warn and require a secondary confirmation for wide-scoped writes.

ci-bot: deploy-check: schema change detected (pin_matrix_v1). Backfill job would run as a k8s cron; ensure DB migration runbook updated.

maria_dev: can we also add soft-fallback hints? e.g., entry can include `fallback_priority` so routing can prefer cheaper variants if under pressure. that ties into smart routing cost policy.

alex_k: yes but keep it optional. default semantics must be simple: matrix entry expresses explicit variant weights OR fixed pin. fallback_priority only used by routing, not by resolver. document that separation.

(taylor_arch): next steps I propose:
- add full proto draft with fields: columns, rows, meta {epoch, compat_ttl, created_by}, exceptions list, fallback_hint
- implement resolver read path: explicit_pin -> exceptions -> matrix -> default
- telemetry keys as suggested
- RBAC + UI warning for writes affecting >N tenants
- perf benchmark on staging with 100k rows

maria_dev: sounds good. please ping infra for perf test infra. also add a small section in runbook for rollbacks: how to quickly revert matrix updates (epoch-based fast revert).

pranav_s: I'll draft the telemetry spec and a small preflight check for writes (ensure no unintentional tenant-wide overwrite).

alex_k: and I'll try to prototype the index map + caching code in the resolver. probably a small in-memory trie keyed by tenant|env.

taylor_arch: awesome — will open an RFC follow-up with the proto + migration options. tagging @maria_dev @alex_k @pranav_s. :thumbsup:

ci-bot: note: thread autosaved to rfc-drafts.
